metricQualityCaveatNeitherSideStates.denominator: changedPixelRatio = changedPixels / OVERLAP pixels, with commonAreaRatio reported separately (src/reconstruction-qa/screenshot-diff.ts:126-127). Honest. On all 8 pairs I recomputed, commonAreaRatio = 1.0000 (heights match exactly), so no full-page-vs-viewport confusion.
metricQualityCaveatNeitherSideStates.tolerance: zero. A pixel counts as changed when ANY channel differs by 1 level.
metricQualityCaveatNeitherSideStates.myRecomputation: I re-derived changedPixelRatio from the shipped snapshot/clone PNGs with my own pngjs script and reproduced the artifact to 4 dp on all 8 pairs (0.2075, 0.1602, 0.4956, 0.4321, 0.0235, 0.0371, 0.3831, 0.3292). The metric is reproducible.

tolerance_sweep.reading: 74% of the changed pixels are <=8 levels - text rasterization noise
cliff between 8 and 16 - a uniform low-amplitude tint offset over ~42% of the page, not antialiasing

metricQualityCaveatNeitherSideStates.consequence: the wave-1 headline range 0.0235..0.4953 and the 16.79% median are ZERO-TOLERANCE changed-pixel counts. They conflate text rasterization noise with a low-amplitude uniform colour offset. They are an upper bound on visible wrongness, not a share of the page that looks wrong.
